evidence.effect: 10-year auction day, ZN futures decline ahead of the auction
evidence.rule: ZN short ahead of 10Y auction, long after (window unstated)
evidence.conversion: 6 bp of ZN price / 1.42 bp per tick (price 110 assumption)
evidence.sample: US 10-year T-Note futures, Tickdata, 1983-01..2024-08, 382 million transactions
evidence.source: Houweling, Penninga, Martinetti (Robeco), Quant chart: US Treasuries up for auction, 2025-03-27
evidence.quote: The intraday chart in Figure 1 illustrates a clear pattern: ahead of the auction, on average futures prices decline by 6 basis points, only to recover in the hours that follow.

evidence.rule: trade in the direction of the later surprise from release-30 min (not causal: needs the surprise sign)
evidence.decay_evidence: 'the price drift has increased since 2007'; post-2015 unknown
evidence.source: Kurov, Sancetta, Strasser, Wolfe, ECB WP 1901 (2016); JFQA 54 (2019)
evidence.quote: This drift accounts for 49 per- cent and 39 percent of the overall price adjustments in the E-mini S&P 500 and 10-year Treasury note futures markets, respectively; ... some drift (only about one basis point) ...; The median bid-ask spread is 0.020% for the E-mini S&P 500 futures and 0.013% for 10-year Treasury notes futures.

evidence.conversion: null result (10-year coefficient < 1 bp, significant only at 10% in 1980-2011)
evidence.source: Lucca and Moench, The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift, FRBNY SR 512 (rev. 2013); JF 2015
evidence.quote: we find no such effect in U.S. Treasury securities and money market futures. ... For the 1980-2011 sample the on-the-run ten-year Treasury is significant at the 10% level with a coefficient of less than a basis point.

evidence.effect: Post-FOMC drift in long bond futures
evidence.rule: long after expansionary, short after contractionary FOMC shocks
evidence.sample: post-GFC transaction-level US and German long bond futures
evidence.source: Indriawan, Jiao, Tse (2021), J. Banking & Finance 123, 106027
evidence.quote: we observe a sizable post-announcement drift in government bond markets. A trading strategy of investing in the market after expansionary shocks and shorting the market following contractionary surprises yields up to four times the Sharpe ratio of buy-and-hold investment.

evidence.effect: End-of-month Treasury futures returns (close-to-close, not intraday)
evidence.rule: long 10Y futures over the last t days of the month
evidence.conversion: 0.09 percentage points = 9 bp (last day); /1.42; includes overnight, so not an intraday figure
evidence.source: Hartley and Schwarz (2019), Predictable End-of-Month Treasury Returns, Wharton Rodney White Center WP
evidence.quote: 10-Year 0.09*** 0.14*** 0.17*** 0.18*** 0.22*** 0.20*** -0.06 -0.08* -0.10** -0.04 ... The units are (approximate) percentage points per month ... The sample period is from 1990 to 2018.

evidence.effect: Month-end index strike time (activity, no returns)
evidence.decay_evidence: strike moved 3 pm to 4 pm ET in January 2021
evidence.source: Dyer, Fleming, Shachar, Treasury Trading at the Close, Liberty Street Economics, 2026-09-22
evidence.quote: We also document a marked shift in trading activity from around 3 p.m. (ET) to around 4 p.m. after a major fixed-income index provider moved its strike time from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m. in January 2021.

evidence.effect: First-15 to last-15 minute momentum, Chinese Treasury bond futures
evidence.rule: sign of first 15-min return -> last 15 min
evidence.sample: CFFEX Treasury bond futures (years not seen)
evidence.source: Zhang, Wang, Li (2021), Bond intraday momentum, J. Behavioral and Experimental Finance 31
evidence.quote: By utilizing high-frequency data from the Chinese Treasury bond futures market, we find that the first fifteen-minute return is a good predictor of the last fifteen-minute return.
